Usually the right answer, and the cheapest one
Nitrile has been the standard shaft-seal compound for decades. If your shaft runs in oil below +120 °C and is not exposed to weather, you do not need anything dearer — and we will say so.

Higher acrylonitrile resists oil better and stiffens sooner in the cold; lower stays flexible and swells more. We mix our own compounds, so tell us the medium and the coldest start temperature and we set it between them.
Nitrile cracks in ozone and UV — the commonest mistake made with it. If the shaft is outdoors or on exposed plant, specify neoprene where oil resistance still matters, or EPDM where it does not.

Compound datasheets and dimensioned drawings are issued on request, under NDA where required. Send shaft diameter, housing bore, width and the medium, and we will confirm the type and nitrile content against them.
What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes. Send the old seal and, if you can, tell us how it failed — a hardened, cracked lip means heat or ozone, a grooved lip means abrasive contamination, and a polished band on the shaft means the shaft is the problem, not the seal. We size from the housing and the shaft, not from the worn part.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?

PDF, DWG, DXF and STEP — but a drawing is often unnecessary. Shaft diameter, housing bore, width, type A or AS, plus the medium and the temperature range is a complete specification. State the coldest start temperature separately — it sets the nitrile content.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412 and compression set to ASTM D395 Method B are tested in-house, with dimensions checked against DIN 3760.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?

TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Seals are packed to protect the sealing lip.
